dedupe_keys.name: building damage datasets for the 2023 turkiye earthquake

description: This dataset gathers building footprints, post-earthquake building damage assessments and geo-environmental factors for the region hit by the February 2023 earthquakes in Türkiye, to support research on identifying and predicting building damage. It was compiled by Haihui Liu and published on Zenodo on 31 January 2026. Coverage is the affected provinces of south-eastern Türkiye. It has three parts: building footprint polygons for the affected regions taken from GlobalBuildingAtlas; damage evaluations from five sources (NASA ARIA damage proxy maps from Sentinel-1 radar, UNOSAT expert damage grades, Microsoft's AI-assisted assessments, manually interpreted labels used as high-confidence validation, and the author's own results); and rasters of elevation, distance to the epicentre, distance to faults, lithology and peak ground velocity. Access: one zip archive of about 585 MB, open download. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the compilation; component sources keep their own terms. Caveats: the damage sources differ in method and grading, so they disagree, and the footprints are machine-derived. Simulation uses are calibrating and validating seismic damage and fragility models, and training remote-sensing damage classifiers. Related records: GlobalBuildingAtlas and post-earthquake reconnaissance datasets.
